name: What is included in commercial construction closeout?

mainEntity.name: What documents and tasks are usually required to close out a commercial construction project?
mainEntity.text: What documents and tasks are usually required to close out a commercial construction project?

acceptedAnswer.text: Closeout is the final phase that turns a finished job into an approved one. It usually includes final inspections, resolution of punch-list items, submittal of as-builts, product manuals, warranty information, training on systems, and any required lien releases or completion paperwork. In commercial projects, closeout also means securing final permit sign-off and making sure all agencies that touched the project have completed their review. Owners sometimes underestimate closeout because the space looks done, but occupancy or financing may still depend on paperwork and final approvals. A good contractor should track closeout items from the beginning so the project does not get stuck at the finish line.
acceptedAnswer.description: Commercial closeout usually includes final inspections, correction completion, as-builts, manuals, warranties, lien releases, and permit sign-off. The project is not fully finished until the building department and other required agencies have closed their items.
